meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start there.
I'm waiting. Who decided to enter that zero before anyone spoke to me?
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?
You're leading me, and I've done this for twenty years. I asked who decided to enter that zero before anyone called me.
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?
That's the second one, and I'm not answering hypotheticals about my son. How Owen spends his evenings has nothing to do with why that zero went in before anyone picked up a phone.
So it's at least possible he used it once?
No. I'm writing down that you've asked me three leading questions and haven't shown me one document. Either you put something on this desk, or I'm going upstairs to the principal.
That's not what I said, and you know it. Show me a document or I'm going upstairs.
